column1: # Open findings of the fuzz harnesses (dm/tools/fuzz/fuzzlib.py), one row per cause: harness, signature pattern (fnmatch, alternatives separated by |), its inputs in corpus/<harness>/ (comma-separated), issue, what

column5: name() reads the u16 size of a compressed title area from a file shorter than 2 bytes
Image() unpacks the 32-byte header from an image cut short after its magic
nso_image allocates the image the header lays out (data offset + size, up to 8 GiB) before checking it against the file
mshd_shaders hands a code area shorter than its 0x34-byte header to sph_stage
magic_back seeks before the start of a file shorter than a footer
bnsh_shaders follows the variation table pointer (u64 at +0x80) unchecked; one past the C index range raises OverflowError
Pak reads the index (mount point, entry count, entries) without checking it against the index size from the footer: an empty or short index raises struct.error

a stored (uncompressed) segment shorter than its size is accepted: the slice assignment shrinks the image, so it comes out shorter than the header lays out (or, for text or ro, with the next segments shifted); no error
yaz0 decodes until the size in its header without checking the input end: a Yaz0 stream cut short raises IndexError
Pak.read_at reads the directory index size from the index unchecked: a size past 2^63 raises OverflowError from f.read
sdf_shaders follows an entry's stage offsets and lengths unchecked: one past the end raises struct.error instead of a red line
Pak.read_at reads as many bytes as the footer's index size says before checking it against the file: f.read allocates that size up front, so a huge one raises MemoryError
sarc_members reads the SARC and SFAT headers and the entry table unchecked: a SARC cut short raises struct.error
lslg reads the code length at control +0x704 without checking that the control section is there: a record that ends inside it raises struct.error instead of returning None
glslc_shaders reads control +0x20 and +0x704 of a control section found inside the output without checking that the section is there: an output cut inside it raises struct.error

the compression method of an entry indexes the footer's method names unchecked (a legacy index's flags past 7, a version 11 entry's 6-bit method past the 5 names): IndexError; a negative legacy flag silently picks a name from the end of the list
arh_entries checks that the path prefix from the trie is ASCII but decodes the suffix from the string table unchecked: a non-ASCII byte raises UnicodeDecodeError instead of a red line

lz4_shaders passes a shader entry's raw size (u32, up to 4 GiB) to lz4.block.decompress, which allocates it up front, without checking it against the compressed size (LZ4 expands at most about 255 times)

Pak checks for a key only when the index is encrypted: reading a file whose entry has the encrypted bit (22) without a key calls aes_decrypt(None, ...) (TypeError on macOS; on Linux, where CommonCrypto is missing, OSError)
tfxo_shaders reads control +0x704 of a control section that ends early: a .tfxo file cut inside a control section raises struct.error instead of a red line
archive unpacks the shader index array with the count from the archive unchecked: a count past the end raises struct.error instead of ValueError

scan_blob reads the size of every 'BNSH\\0\\0\\0\\0' match at +0x1c without checking that the header is there: the magic within 0x20 bytes of the end of any scanned file raises struct.error and the file's other shaders are left out

scan_blob expands SARC members without checking that a member lies inside the archive and is smaller than it: a member that spans the whole SARC is scanned as itself until RecursionError, copying the archive at each of ~1000 levels (a 50 MB archive: ~50 GB)
a legacy (version 4) entry's data offset is a signed i64 used unchecked: a negative one makes Pak.read_at seek before the file start (OSError EINVAL)
bahs_shaders reads the code region fields at +0x18 / +0x1c without checking the header is there: a BAHS file shorter than 0x20 bytes raises struct.error
Pak.read passes an entry's raw size (block size) to lz4.block.decompress, which allocates it up front, without checking it against the stored size
